title: Forensic Toxicology
sources_used: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Mention two examples of antidotes used in poisoning cases.
questions.solution_html:
• Any two appropriate examples, e.g., naloxone for opioid toxicity; atropine plus pralidoxime for organophosphate poisoning
  • One further correct antidote/toxin pairing, e.g., N-acetylcysteine for paracetamol; deferoxamine for iron (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: • One further correct antidote/toxin pairing, e.g., N-acetylcysteine for paracetamol; deferoxamine for iron

questions.question: A forensic sample is suspected to contain a phosphide compound. Which preliminary chemical test would you select and what is its purpose?
questions.solution_html:
• A suitable preliminary test for phosphide/phosphine, such as a validated silver-nitrate paper test for liberated phosphine
  • may be selected (1 mark)
  • Purpose is presumptive screening; specify safe, controlled handling and confirmatory analysis as appropriate (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: • Purpose is presumptive screening; specify safe, controlled handling and confirmatory analysis as appropriate

questions.question: What is meant by evidence material in food-poisoning investigation?
questions.solution_html:
• Materials collected to investigate suspected food poisoning, e.g., leftover food, vomitus, gastric contents, stool, blood or
  • suspected container (1 mark)
  • Proper labelling, preservation, representative sampling and chain of custody are essential (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: • Proper labelling, preservation, representative sampling and chain of custody are essential

questions.question: Mention two signs of carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.solution_html:
• Any two: headache, dizziness, nausea, weakness, confusion, syncope (1 mark)
  • Severe cases may show seizures/coma; cherry-red colour is uncommon and should not be relied on (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: • Severe cases may show seizures/coma; cherry-red colour is uncommon and should not be relied on

questions.question: How can the Dithionite test be applied to Paraquat or Diquat examination?
questions.solution_html:
• Sodium dithionite in alkaline conditions reduces paraquat/diquat to coloured radical species (paraquat commonly blue) — 1
  • Presumptive screening only; confirm with a specific validated instrumental method (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: • Presumptive screening only; confirm with a specific validated instrumental method

questions.question: What are plant poisons?
questions.solution_html:
• Toxic substances naturally occurring in plants (1 mark)
  • Examples include alkaloids, glycosides or toxic plant constituents such as oleandrin/odollam-related cardiac glycosides — 1
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: mark

questions.question: Differentiate between the analysis of ethyl alcohol in beverages and biological fluids.
questions.solution_html:
• Beverages: usually direct measurement of ethanol in the drink, with matrix/dilution considerations (1 mark)
  • Biological fluids: validated forensic method (often headspace GC) with matrix effects, preservation, calibration and
  • interpretation considerations (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: interpretation considerations

questions.question: Explain the use of spectrophotometry in poison analysis.
questions.solution_html:
• Measures absorption of light at selected wavelengths to estimate analyte concentration or support identification (1 mark)
  • Useful for suitable compounds/reactions; selectivity is limited and confirmation may be needed (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: • Measures absorption of light at selected wavelengths to estimate analyte concentration or support identification

questions.question: Why are instrumental techniques used for identification?
questions.solution_html:
• Provide greater sensitivity, selectivity and reproducibility than many simple screening tests (1 mark)
  • Can separate and identify compounds in mixtures and/or quantify them using validated methods (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: • Provide greater sensitivity, selectivity and reproducibility than many simple screening tests

questions.question: Analyse how the route of ingestion can influence the absorption and distribution of a poison.
questions.solution_html:
• Route affects absorption rate/bioavailability; oral exposure may be affected by dissolution, food and first-pass metabolism
  • Distribution/onset also depend on dose, chemical properties, tissue perfusion and route-specific exposure (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: • Distribution/onset also depend on dose, chemical properties, tissue perfusion and route-specific exposure

questions.question: How can HPLC be applied to poison detection?
questions.solution_html:
• Separates components in a sample based on interactions with stationary and mobile phases (1 mark)
  • Detector response/retention time, preferably with suitable confirmatory detection and standards, supports
  • identification/quantification (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: identification/quantification

questions.question: Explain one limitation of a toxicological method.
questions.solution_html:
• Any valid limitation: matrix interference, limited sensitivity, lack of specificity, detection-window limits, degradation or
  • inability to distinguish exposure from impairment (1 mark)
  • Explain its effect or need for controls/confirmation/validated interpretation (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: • Explain its effect or need for controls/confirmation/validated interpretation

questions.question: Explain the principle and forensic application of the Conway diffusion method for the determination of ethyl alcohol.
questions.solution_html:
• Volatile ethanol diffuses from the outer chamber of a sealed Conway microdiffusion unit (1 mark)
  • Ethanol is absorbed in a suitable receiving reagent in the inner chamber (1 mark)
  • The captured ethanol is determined by a validated chemical/analytical procedure with standards and blanks (1 mark)
  • Used for determination of ethanol in appropriate samples; limitations include diffusion conditions, interference and need for
  • validation (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: validation

questions.question: Analyse the role of preliminary colour tests in forensic toxicology and explain why their results require confirmation by more specific analytical techniques.
questions.solution_html:
• Rapid, inexpensive screening of suspected drugs/poisons (1 mark)
  • Colour reaction can indicate a class or possible analyte, not definitive identity (1 mark)
  • Cross-reactions, matrix effects and subjective colour interpretation can produce false positives/negatives (1 mark)
  • Confirm using validated specific methods such as GC–MS or LC–MS/MS, as appropriate (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: • Confirm using validated specific methods such as GC–MS or LC–MS/MS, as appropriate

questions.question: Describe insect and animal toxins relevant to toxicological analysis.
questions.solution_html:
• Examples of insect toxins/venoms: bee, wasp, ant or other medically relevant venom exposures (1 mark)
  • Examples of animal toxins: snake venom, scorpion venom, marine toxins or toxic secretions (1 mark)
  • Discuss relevant toxic components/effects, e.g., neurotoxic, haemotoxic or cytotoxic action (1 mark)
  • Specimen selection, clinical/history context and validated targeted analysis are important (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: • Specimen selection, clinical/history context and validated targeted analysis are important

questions.question: Analyse how clean-up and concentration procedures improve the reliability of the subsequent identification of drugs and poisons.
questions.solution_html:
• Remove proteins, lipids and other matrix interferences (1 mark)
  • Concentrate trace analytes to improve detection limits (1 mark)
  • Improve chromatographic separation, detector response and reduce instrument contamination (1 mark)
  • Use recovery checks/internal standards and avoid analyte loss or contamination during preparation (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: • Use recovery checks/internal standards and avoid analyte loss or contamination during preparation

questions.question: Explain TLC examination of barbiturates and cannabinoids.
questions.solution_html:
• Extract the sample and apply extract plus reference standards to a suitable TLC plate (1 mark)
  • Develop in a validated solvent system and allow separation (1 mark)
  • Visualize using appropriate detection reagents/UV and compare Rf values and appearance with standards (1 mark)
  • TLC is presumptive; matrix effects and similar Rf values mean confirmation by a specific method is required (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: • TLC is presumptive; matrix effects and similar Rf values mean confirmation by a specific method is required

questions.question: Discuss the presentation of laboratory findings in a toxicological report.
questions.solution_html:
• Identify case/sample details, seals, condition, receipt and chain of custody (1 mark)
  • State methods, controls, calibration/quality assurance and relevant limitations (1 mark)
  • Report results with units, detection/quantification limits where relevant and clear distinction between detected/not detected
  • Give cautious interpretation, avoid unsupported conclusions, and include analyst/date/signature as required (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: • Give cautious interpretation, avoid unsupported conclusions, and include analyst/date/signature as required

questions.question: Analyse the factors that affect the extraction of acidic and basic drugs from viscera, blood, and urine.
questions.solution_html:
• pH and analyte pKa determine ionisation and partitioning (1 mark)
  • Solvent polarity, liquid–liquid or solid-phase extraction conditions and solvent-to-sample ratio (1 mark)
  • Sample matrix, protein binding, metabolites, degradation and storage/preservation (1 mark)
  • Extraction recovery, selectivity, internal standards and validation affect reliability (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: • Extraction recovery, selectivity, internal standards and validation affect reliability

questions.question: Explain the general principles and procedures involved in the extraction and isolation of poisons from biological specimens. Discuss the factors affecting the recovery of poisons
questions.solution_html:
• Selection and documentation of specimens based on case history and suspected poison; preserve chain of custody — 2
  • Preliminary examination/screening and appropriate sample homogenisation or aliquoting (2 marks)
  • Suitable extraction/clean-up strategy (e.g., liquid–liquid, solid-phase, headspace or other method chosen for analyte
  • properties) (2 marks)
  • Isolation/concentration, use of blanks, standards/internal standards and recovery controls (2 marks)
  • Factors: pH/pKa, polarity, binding, matrix, degradation, storage, extraction solvent, technique and analyte volatility; confirm
  • and quantify with validated methods (2 marks)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: and quantify with validated methods

questions.question: Analyse the differences between chemical and bacterial food poisoning with respect to their toxicological examination.
questions.solution_html:
• Chemical food poisoning arises from chemicals/toxins such as pesticides, metals or other toxic substances; bacterial food
  • poisoning arises from pathogenic bacteria or their toxins (2 marks)
  • Case history, symptom onset, food history and epidemiological pattern guide investigation (2 marks)
  • Chemical examination: targeted screening/confirmation and quantification in food and biological specimens using validated
  • chemical/instrumental methods (2 marks)
  • Bacterial examination: microbiological culture, molecular methods and/or toxin assays as appropriate; collect suitable food
  • and clinical specimens (2 marks)
  • Compare evidence, controls, sampling and interpretation; consider preformed toxins, incubation period, specimen
  • degradation and avoid overclaiming from a single positive result (2 marks)
  • Marking note: The paper instructs students to attempt at least one question from each course outcome. Apply the examination
  • regulations when evaluating attempt requirements.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: regulations when evaluating attempt requirements.
